messages:
sophia: Ran the new redwoodctl installer on my Windows laptop this morning. Post-install it seems to drop a shell hook into my profile but the CLI can't find my config/profile when started from Git Bash. Also the interactive login tries to open Edge but nothing happens (no browser window).

mike: Ugh. Can you paste the output of `redwoodctl version` and `redwoodctl auth status --debug`? Also which shell exactly (Git Bash, MSYS, WSL, Powershell)?

sophia: Git Bash (Mintty). Version is `redwoodctl 0.17.4`. auth status output:```
DEBUG: loading config from C:/Users/sophia/AppData/Local/Redwood/cli/config.json
INFO: using profile default -> C:/Users/sophia/.redwood/profile.json
ERROR: env PATH entry points to shortname (C:\PROGRA~1) -> resolved path mismatch
ERROR: open browser failed: spawn cmd ENOENT
```

sam: That spawn error makes sense on MinTTY: it doesn't have cmd.exe shim in PATH like normal consoles. Two options: 1) use PowerShell/Windows Terminal, 2) use headless/device auth.

sophia: Tried Powershell and it works fine there (browser opens). But our dev workflow runs in Git Bash for a local serve script and the postinstall hook added a `source ~/.config/redwood/hook.sh` line into `~/.bashrc` that breaks some prompt behavior in Mintty.

mike: Can you show the hook.sh? Also do you have any antivirus or policy blocking loopback ports? The login flow starts a localhost callback (default 34567) which some AVs block.

sophia: Hook is tiny:```
# redwoodctl shell hook
export REDWOOD_HOME="$HOME/.redwood"
[ -f "$REDWOOD_HOME/env" ] && . "$REDWOOD_HOME/env"
```
No AV on this machine. The kicker: because Git Bash resolves $HOME differently the redwoodctl binary resolves config paths with Windows shortnames, so the hook points at the wrong place.

chris: This is a classic shell-path normalization problem. Two quick fixes: 1) reinstall with the installer flag that creates a Windows-native symlink in C:\Users\sophia\AppData\Local\Redwood\bin instead of relying on the shortname PATH entry, or 2) set REDWOOD_HOME explicitly in your Git Bash ~/.bashrc to the Windows path using /c/Users/sophia style.

sophia: Reinstalled with `redwoodctl-installer --symlink` and added `export REDWOOD_HOME=/c/Users/sophia/.redwood` to ~/.bashrc. That fixed the profile lookup but the login still fails in Mintty (same spawn cmd error).

sam: For the login: use the device flow: `redwoodctl login --device`. It prints a code you paste into a browser session on Windows (works around spawn/xdg-open). We added that specifically for terminals without GUI integration.

sophia: `redwoodctl login --device` worked! Got tokens and `redwoodctl auth status` shows active. Thanks. Leaving this note: postinstall should detect MinTTY and avoid adding the hook automatically (or add a small note), and the installer should prefer symlink mode on Win when PATH contains shortnames.

mike: Filing a devex ticket and tagging infra to consider a safer default. @devex-bot can you create a perf ticket for this behavior (installer: prefer symlink on Windows / detect MinTTY and surface guidance)? :bug:
